the effects of hyperthermia in combination with ionizing radiation are complex and that the response of any tumour subpopulation to this combined treatment is dependent on a number of variables including the sequence of application, temperature and time of exposure to hyperthermia, the dose and linear energy transfer of ionizing radiation, and, perhaps, the inherent biological characteristics of the tumour subpopulation.

A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the combined treatments of hyperthermia with X-irradiations are not always additive or supra-additive in their effects on tumour cells.
hyperthermia is an effective modality for treating tumours, but the response of tumour sub-populations to the combined modality of hyperthermia plus X-irradiations is not necessarily predictable.
the combined modality treatment of hyperthermia with X-irradiations is more effective than either treatment alone.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the responses of the tumour subpopulation to combined modality treatment may be different from that of the bulk tumour.
it is not possible to predict the effects of combined treatments on heterogeneous tumours based on the responses of the bulk tumour population.

, while it is important to understand the mechanisms of combined modality treatments, it is equally important to understand the heterogeneity of tumour cell populations and their responses to combined modality treatment.
